investigations.title: Who funds the opposition to the Ridgeline Act?
investigations.question: Four delegates voted NO on HB-14 against their districts' air-quality and just-transition interests. Is there a money pattern behind the opposition?
investigations.findings: A corroborated donor→PAC→vote pattern accounts for three of the four NO votes: Ridge Coal Legacy Trust (and, pending corroboration, Blackwater Holdings) fund the Cumberland Energy Action Fund, which contributes to Boyd, Tipton, and Crane — all three NO. The fourth NO, Delegate Hale, takes no Cumberland money; his opposition rests on Title I's land and water provisions. The money explains the bloc, not the whole vote — not all opposition is bought.

evidence_cards.claim: Ridge Coal Legacy Trust funds the Cumberland Energy Action Fund.
Cumberland Energy Action Fund contributes to Delegate Harlan Boyd.
Cumberland Energy Action Fund contributes to Delegate Eli Tipton.
Cumberland Energy Action Fund contributes to Delegate Theo Crane.
Boyd, Tipton, and Crane — the three Cumberland-funded delegates — all voted NO on HB-14.
Blackwater Holdings LLC shares an officer, Dell Aldridge, with the Cumberland Energy Action Fund — suggesting a second, indirect funding path.
evidence_cards.note: INFERRED link — held un-promotable pending independent corroboration. Demonstrates the citation discipline: a plausible claim that the system will not let advance to a graph edge on one inferred source.

evidence_cards.claim: The fourth NO vote, Delegate Marcus Hale, takes no Cumberland money; his stated opposition is to Title I's land and water provisions.
evidence_cards.note: The control case — the money explains the bloc, not Hale. Keeps the investigation honest.
